question.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.40.$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $\,p\,$ | $0.10$ | $0.15$ | $0.20$ | $0.25$ | $0.30$ | $0.35$ | $0.40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ | $\,-0.5244\,$ | $\,-0.3853\,$ | $\,-0.2533\,$ |

$z=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given information in terms of $Φ:$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\le z) & =0.40 \\ Φ(z) & =0.40\end{aligned}
$$

So, we are looking for the value of $z$ such that

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.40).
$$

We look for the column in the table that corresponds to $p=0.40,$ and we find that

$$
p=0.40\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)=-0.2533.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.40)=-0.2533.
$$
